title: Preparation of an alteration problem as a relative curve
statement:
Let $S$ be either the spectrum of a field or an excellent integral trait (the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring), with generic point $s$. Let $X\to S$ be a proper dominant finite-type morphism with $X$ integral and $d=\dim X_s\geq1$. Let $Z\subset X$ be a nowhere dense closed subscheme, meaning that its underlying closed set contains no generic point of $X$. There are excellent integral schemes $X_1,Y$, a proper dominant generically finite $S$-morphism $h:X_1\to X$, a projective [def-kun-projective], proper, dominant finite-type morphism $Y\to S$ with $\dim Y_s=d-1$, and a proper dominant morphism $f:X_1\to Y$ such that the structure map of $X_1$ is the composite through $Y$. If $y$ is the generic point of $Y$, then $(X_1)_y$ is a smooth irreducible curve and $((h^{-1}Z)_{\mathrm{red}})_y$ is finite etale over $\kappa(y)$ (possibly empty). Here generically finite means finite over a dense open in the target; the degree is unrestricted. Excellence means excellence of affine coordinate rings.

Conventions for the notions used here: properness [def-weil-proper-morphism]; finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; integrality [def-pc-integral-scheme]; excellence [def-exc-excellent-ring]; discrete valuation rings [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]; smoothness [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; etaleness [def-weil-etale-morphism]; reduction [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]; scheme-theoretic fibres [def-pc-scheme-fibre]; dimension [def-kun-dimension]; closed subschemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]; finite morphisms [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; projectivity [def-kun-projective].

source.place: Expose X, proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 2 (projective reduction) and Step 5 (factorization through a relative curve and inseparable preparation), printed pp. 162--164; take the reduced inverse image of the boundary. Step 5 makes $h:Y\to S$ projective and the inseparable alteration $Y'\to Y$ projective; since $S$ is affine, these are projective in the closed-immersion-into-$\mathbf P^N$ convention by Stacks 087S (morphisms-lemma-projective-over-quasi-projective-is-H-projective) and 01WE (morphisms-lemma-H-projective-composition).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-relative-curve-factorization] to the given proper dominant finite-type $X\to S$ with $X$ integral and $\dim X_s=d\geq1$. It supplies an excellent integral $Y_0$ with a projective dominant finite-type morphism $Y_0\to S$ and $\dim(Y_0)_s=d-1$, an excellent integral $X_0$, a proper dominant generically finite $a:X_0\to X$ and a proper dominant $g:X_0\to Y_0$ with equal composites $X_0\to X\to S$ and $X_0\to Y_0\to S$, and $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(Y_0)}\kappa(X_0)=1$.

source.place: Expose X, proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 5, printed p. 163

proof.text: These are exactly the hypotheses of [lem-trf-generic-smooth-boundary-preparation] (with $Y=Y_0$), together with the given nowhere dense $Z\subset X$. It gives an excellent integral $Y_1$ with a projective proper dominant generically finite $b:Y_1\to Y_0$, the composite $Y_1\to S$ projective, $\kappa(Y_1)/\kappa(Y_0)$ finite purely inseparable; an excellent integral $X_1$ with $c:X_1\to X_0$, $f:X_1\to Y_1$, $g\circ c=b\circ f$, $h=a\circ c$ proper dominant generically finite, $f$ proper dominant; and, at the generic point $y_1$ of $Y_1$, a smooth irreducible curve $(X_1)_{y_1}$ and a finite etale $((h^{-1}Z)_{\mathrm{red}})_{y_1}$.

source.place: Expose X, proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 5, printed pp. 163–164

proof.text: Put $Y=Y_1$ and $y=y_1$. The structure map of $X_1$ is the composite through $Y$, and $h$ is an $S$-morphism: $(X\to S)\circ a\circ c=(Y_0\to S)\circ g\circ c=(Y_0\to S)\circ b\circ f$. The morphism $Y\to S$ is projective by step 2, hence proper by [lem-pc-projective-proper] (and so of finite type); it is dominant as the composite of the dominant maps $b$ and $Y_0\to S$ (elementary: the generic point of $Y$ goes to that of $Y_0$, then to $s$). For the dimension: $Y$ is integral and dominates $S$, so $Y_s$ is a finite-type $\kappa(s)$-scheme whose underlying set is the set of points of $Y$ over $s$; it contains the generic point of $Y$, whose closure in $Y_s$ is all of $Y_s$ and whose residue field is $\kappa(Y)$. [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg] with $C=Y_s$ gives $\dim Y_s=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(Y)$, and likewise $\dim (Y_0)_s=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(Y_0)=d-1$. Since $\kappa(Y)/\kappa(Y_0)$ is finite, hence algebraic, a transcendence basis of $\kappa(Y_0)$ over $\kappa(s)$ is one of $\kappa(Y)$ (elementary), so $\dim Y_s=d-1$. The remaining clauses are those of step 2 verbatim.

lean.statement: theorem alteration_relative_curve_preparation (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (hbase : IsField A ∨ ∃ hD : IsDomain A, Nonempty (@IsDiscreteValuationRing A inferInstance hD) ∧ IsExcellent A) (S : Scheme.{u}) (eS : S = Spec (.of A)) (s : S) (hs : IsGenericPoint s Set.univ) (X : Scheme.{u}) (p : X ⟶ S) [IsIntegral X] (hp : IsProper p) (hdom : DenseRange p.base) (hft : LocallyOfFiniteType p ∧ QuasiCompact p) (d : ℕ) (hd : topologicalKrullDim (p.fiber s) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) (hdpos : 1 ≤ d) (Z : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] (hZ : ∀ ξ : X, IsGenericPoint ξ Set.univ → ξ ∉ Set.range i.base) : ∃ (X₁ Y : Scheme.{u}) (h : X₁ ⟶ X) (q : Y ⟶ S) (f : X₁ ⟶ Y), IsIntegral X₁ ∧ (∀ U : X₁.Opens, IsAffineOpen U → IsExcellent Γ(X₁, U)) ∧ IsIntegral Y ∧ (∀ U : Y.Opens, IsAffineOpen U → IsExcellent Γ(Y, U)) ∧ IsProper h ∧ DenseRange h.base ∧ (∃ U : X.Opens, Dense (U : Set X) ∧ IsFinite (h ∣_ U)) ∧ IsHProjective q ∧ IsProper q ∧ DenseRange q.base ∧ (LocallyOfFiniteType q ∧ QuasiCompact q) ∧ topologicalKrullDim (q.fiber s) = ((d - 1 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) ∧ IsProper f ∧ DenseRange f.base ∧ h ≫ p = f ≫ q ∧ (∀ y : Y, IsGenericPoint y Set.univ → SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (f.fiberToSpecResidueField y) ∧ IsIntegral (f.fiber y) ∧ IsFinite (((((Limits.pullback h i).nilradical.subschemeι ≫ Limits.pullback.fst h i) ≫ f).fiberToSpecResidueField y)) ∧ Etale (((((Limits.pullback h i).nilradical.subschemeι ≫ Limits.pullback.fst h i) ≫ f).fiberToSpecResidueField y)))
